capabilities: insert hierarchical numbering prefixes like 1.1.1. with trailing periods
create the next sibling item on Enter, or exit numbering on a prefix-only item
indent and outdent items or selected subtrees with Tab and Shift+Tab
insert, delete, and renumber a contiguous numbered block in one undoable transaction
normalize legacy four-space or tab-indented blocks via a renumber command
disambiguation: Not a Markdown list formatter; it treats numbering prefixes like 1.1. as literal text, not as Markdown list markers.
extras: The README notes it is a Community directory submission candidate (release 0.3.4); screenshots, detailed examples, and troubleshooting live in the project Wiki rather than the README. It is local-only with no network requests or telemetry.
intentEvidence: Unlike standard Markdown ordered lists, this plugin owns the entire numeric prefix.
motivation: The README's 'Why this plugin?' section explains that Markdown only recognizes single-integer list markers, so the plugin manages the complete hierarchy as readable plain text and recalculates blocks in one undoable transaction.
problem: Markdown only recognizes a single integer like 1. as an ordered-list marker, so deeper hierarchies such as 1.1. and 1.1.1. cannot be written as stable plain-text numbering.

relations.evidence: Recognized numbering is handled before conflicting Outliner keymaps.

summary: Plugin that creates and maintains hierarchical plain-text numbering such as 1.1.1. with a trailing period at every depth.
